knowledge_gaps: The lexical index is underspecified: define tokenization for hyphenated model identifiers, TF-IDF weighting and normalization, vocabulary limits, catalog ordering, numerical precision, and deterministic top-128 retrieval. The proposed mechanism is uncertain: title similarity need not imply high neural scores or distinguish compatibility. Because titles affect sampling only, the model cannot directly learn shared textual attributes. Report lexical coverage, realized replacement fraction, neural-score hardness, and training-frequency concentration without treating them as selection metrics.

Experimental execution assumes host support for repeated checkpoint evaluation, although only post-training evaluation is guaranteed. Specify the supported evaluation schedule, same-epoch four-category checkpoint bundles, remaining budget allocation, and behavior when no common checkpoint is available.

Reproducibility requires explicit ordered negative sampling, matched initialization and example streams across conditions, RNG derivations, exact terminal-index bounds, and loss-preserving microbatch backward. Chunking scores alone does not guarantee bounded autograd memory.

The 0.5737 historical combined_score is not established as a configuration-matched macro validation HR@10 result. The two-condition experiment isolates lexical replacement, but cannot establish benefits from the retained terminal objective or a curriculum; its fixed mixture is not a curriculum.

Originality 4 is plausible for an incremental adaptation. Potential 7 and difficulty 3 are optimistic without title-coverage and runtime evidence. No evidence presently favors replacing this focused comparison with a more complex architecture.
